title: The Hydrogen Atom, Honestly
blurb: One electron, one proton, and every liberty I take with the picture.

steps.title: Start with the only atom I can solve
body: One electron, one proton, and a potential that goes as 1 over r. This is the last atom in the periodic table with a closed-form answer, and everything I am about to show you is that answer rather than a fit to it.
My cloud is a hundred thousand points I drew from the exact probability density. I tuned nothing here to look right.

steps.title: A probability, not a shell
body: There is no orbit and no surface. The electron has a probability of being found anywhere, and my cloud is that probability drawn as density.

I am showing the nucleus at true scale now, which is why you cannot see it. At this magnification a proton is well under a pixel across, and the marker I show by default is a labelled visual liberty rather than a size.

steps.title: n sets the size, l sets the shape
body: Same n, different l. I draw the 2s as a ball with a gap inside it and the 2p as two lobes, and that gap is a real node: a surface where the electron is never found.
The mean radius moves too. I put the 2s at 318 pm and the 2p at 265 pm, so the rounder state is also the bigger one.

steps.title: Same energy, different shape
body: Those two states look nothing alike, and I put them at exactly the same -3.40 eV. Nothing about their shapes says they should be there.

This is the accidental degeneracy, and accidental is the right word: it belongs to the 1 over r potential and to nothing else. Put a second electron in the way to screen the nucleus and it breaks immediately, which is why I cannot show you this for any other atom.

steps.title: m, and a basis is a choice
body: The chemistry orbitals you were taught, p_x and p_y, are not more real than the complex states with definite m. They are sums of them, and which set you call the answer is a choice of basis rather than a fact about the atom.
I treat both as first-class, and my badge says which one you are looking at. Switch it and watch the same physics wear a different face.

steps.title: A surface is a contour, not a boundary
body: Textbook orbital pictures draw a surface and leave you to assume the electron is inside it. Mine encloses 90% of the electron, and I say so, because the other 10% is genuinely outside and goes on forever.
Drag the fraction and I breathe the surface in and out. There is no radius at which the atom stops.

steps.title: So the degeneracy was my model's lie
body: Turn on fine structure and the level I drew as one line becomes several. The 2s and the 2p were never exactly equal; the model that told you so had left three things out.
My badge changes from EXACT to APPROXIMATION, and it names what I am missing rather than implying I am missing nothing. This is an alpha-squared perturbation, correct to that order and no further.

steps.title: Dirac, exactly, and the gap it still leaves
body: The Dirac equation solves hydrogen in closed form, relativity included, so I go back to EXACT here. It gives me the fine structure my perturbation was approximating.

It is still not the measured answer. I make the 2s and 2p at the same j exactly degenerate and the laboratory does not, and that difference is the Lamb shift. I do not model it, and I say so rather than quietly closing the gap.

steps.title: Levels become lines
body: Every arrow I draw between two levels is a photon, and its wavelength is fixed by the gap. I get 121.57 nm for the 2 to 1 transition and 656.47 nm for the 3 to 2, the red line in every hydrogen discharge tube you have seen.
The dots on the axis are vendored NIST measurements, not a fit of mine. My residual panel shows me agreeing with them, which is the only reason to believe anything above.

steps.title: What my picture cost
body: Every badge on this screen is a claim about how much to trust what is next to it. EXACT means I solved the stated model in closed form. APPROXIMATION means I name my assumptions. VISUAL LIBERTY means the choice was presentational and I disclose it anyway.

My nucleus marker is a liberty. My colour map is a liberty. My point size is a liberty. None of them changes a number, and I label all of them, because a picture that hides its choices is a picture you cannot check.
